NVDA.rationale: NVIDIA's fundamental health is exceptional: Q3 FY2026 revenue of $57.01B accelerated +22.0% QoQ, gross margins reached 73.4%, operating margins 63.2%, ROE 86.5%, and the balance sheet carries near-zero leverage (debt/equity 0.071x from Q3 balance sheet). The franchise is a near-monopoly in AI accelerators (~80-92% market share) with a self-reinforcing CUDA software ecosystem of 5M+ developers. Q4 FY2026 results confirmed continued momentum ($68.1B revenue, +73% YoY, EPS beat by 5.32%), and Q1 FY2027 guidance of $78B revenue with 74.9% gross margins signals the ramp is intact. China H200 sales have resumed, and the Vera Rubin product cycle provides a multi-year growth runway. However, valuation is the binding constraint: trailing PE of 56.6x sits at the 92nd percentile of the observed range (highest of 12 sparse-history points), with an earnings yield of 1.8% a full 254 bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.34%. The stock is priced for near-flawless execution. Macro headwinds are material: WTI crude at $99.27 (+64% over 90 days) threatens hyperscaler capex budgets, and tightening financial conditions (T10Y2Y spread narrowed to 0.51%) add risk. The forward P/E of ~22-24x is more reasonable and provides some valuation cushion, but the trailing multiple leaves limited margin of safety. Near-term catalysts exist (Q1 FY2027 earnings, Vera Rubin ramp, China revenue reopening) but are partially priced in given the stock's 11-day winning streak and proximity to all-time highs ($199.64 vs $212.19 peak). Net: outstanding business, stretched valuation, moderate near-term catalyst support — mildly to moderately attractive.
